overall: At 02:45 ET Atlanta is sitting at 64.4°F with a running max of 66.2°F — typical early-morning conditions for early June with no warming momentum yet (velocity flat at 0.0°F/hr). The dewpoint of 62.6°F is nearly equal to air temperature, indicating near-saturated, foggy conditions that may slow the morning warm-up but are unlikely to suppress the afternoon high significantly.
forecast_obs_notes: Model guidance is in unusually tight agreement: GFS and HRRR are locked together at 85.4°F, NBM blends to 84.1°F, and ECMWF comes in slightly cooler at 83.8°F — a spread of only ~1.6°F across all four models, which lends moderate confidence to the 84–85°F range. The ensemble tails (87–89°F) carry only 5–14% probability and are flagged Tier 4 (Avoid), suggesting low risk of an upside surprise.
max_temp_prediction: The bulk of evidence points to a high in the mid-84s°F. The ECMWF/NBM cluster near 83.8–84.1°F while GFS/HRRR push to 85.4°F; weighting the more conservative ECMWF and the blended NBM slightly higher given the humid, near-saturated morning airmass (which can mute solar heating), a target near 84.5°F is most defensible. Confidence is moderate-to-good given tight model agreement, though the high humidity introduces some uncertainty around convective afternoon cloud cover that could shave a degree off the peak.
